Notes: Earliest documented Jewish presence at Gorgippia (modern Anapa): manumission inscription IBosp 1123 = IJO I BS 20 = IPontEux II 400 (AGRW 83), white marble slab found in Anapa, now in the Hermitage, dated Bosporan year 338 month Deios (Oct.-Nov. 41 CE) under King [Mithridates] (name erased). Pothos son of Strabon dedicates his house-born slave Chrysa to the prayer-house (proseuche) to Theos Hypsistos, 'all-powerful' and 'blessed', ending with an oath by Zeus, Earth and Sun. Identified as Judean (following Levinskaya 1996, 239-240 no. 7) because of 'blessed' (eulogetos) together with the proseuche. Suggests an organized Jewish community with its own prayer-house; no size given. Basis of Year Established. (Jewish Encyclopedia 1906 claims of Jewish settlement in the Bosporus from the 4th c. BCE concern the kingdom in general, not Gorgippia, and are not used.)

Dissenting/older interpretation of the same Gorgippia inscription of Bosporan year 338 (41 CE): the Jewish Encyclopedia (1906, 'Bosporus, Cimmerian') calls it a pagan inscription but says the Biblical name of God at its head shows the influence exercised by the Jews upon their fellow-citizens (the Russian Evreiskaya Entsiklopediya gives the same view, dating it 40 CE). Indicates Jewish influence/presence in or near Gorgippia; no count. (Ustinova 1999 argues the Bosporan Theos Hypsistos cult had no Jewish affiliation - see unavailable list.)

Encyclopaedia Judaica ('Anapa'): Jews settled in ancient Anapa during the rule of King Mithridates (first century CE). Year = c. midpoint of the reign of Mithridates (VIII) of Bosporus, c. 39-45 CE; the statement is probably based on the 41 CE inscription. Settlement event; no figure.

Fragmentary manumission IBosp 1124 = IJO I BS 23 (AGRW 'Manumission (frag.) of a Slave by Judeans'), white marble plaque found near Anapa, now in the Hermitage, dated 59/60 CE under King Cotys (I). A man with his wife frees a (threptos) slave; the restored word 'Ioudaiou[s]' after '[to geno]s' (of the Judean ethnic group) is uncertain. If the restoration holds, it documents Jews 'by race' at Gorgippia c. 60 CE (also cited by Wikipedia 'Anapa' after Collar 2013). No count.

Tertiary wiki article (cyclowiki, 'Jewish community of Anapa') states that ancient Gorgippia had a Jewish community, a synagogue and a Jewish cemetery, that Judaism apparently spread among local pagans, that local Jews engaged in trade, and that the Judean inscriptions date to 41, 56, 68, 93 and 124 CE (Russian translation published by A. Harkavy 1865). The 68 CE text corresponds to the manumission by Neokles son of Athenodoros (SEG 19.504, Bosporan-era date 67/68 CE, reign of Rhescuporis I), which could not be fetched. Weak source; the 56 CE date could not be verified and the 93/124 CE dates are outside the period. Organized community; no count.
